part.text:
The images are ready. Your workspace defines exactly one view, so there's one file:

- **`/work/SystemContext.svg`** — the `SystemContext` view (Patron → Library, "Browses the catalogue through" [HTTPS]), drawn in standard C4 style: person in `#084270`, software system in `#1168bd`, left-to-right layout per the view's `autoLayout`, with title and legend.

One transparency note: this sandbox has no network access (DNS fails for every host, including package mirrors), no root, and no JVM/Node/Python/Graphviz — so a standard renderer (structurizr-cli/PlantUML) couldn't be installed or run. Instead I parsed the DSL with the structurizr tools, exported the view's exact elements/relationships, and generated the SVG directly from that data. It's well-formed XML and opens in any browser or image viewer.

If you specifically need PNG, the options are: run this in an environment with network access (I'd install PlantUML or use the Kroki service), or convert the SVG with any local tool you have (`rsvg-convert`, Inkscape, or a browser screenshot).
